summary: Arthur Schopenhauer worked in philosophy. He studied at Ernestinum Gotha (~1807), University of Göttingen (1809), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1811). He later held posts at the University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1820–1831).

Indologist Arthur W. Ryder studied at Harvard (~1894–1901) under Charles Rockwell Lanman and at Leipzig University (~1901–1902) under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Instructor in Sanskrit at Harvard (~1902–1906) and Professor at the University of California (~1906–1938).

Arthur Waley worked in sinology, japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rugby School (~1903–1907), King's College (~1907–1910), and under Gustav Haloun. He held posts at the British Museum (1913) and SOAS University of London.
Aruna Haldar was a scholar in indology and philosophy who studied under Kedar Nath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose. She later held a teaching post at Patna University.

Indologist Arunoday Natvarlal Jani studied under M. V. Upadhyay and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Mumbai (~1947–1953) under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He was Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Baroda College (attested 1957).

Arvind Sharma works in religious studies, indology, and philosophy. He studied at Allahabad, Syracuse, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard. He held posts at Queensland (~1976–1980), Harvard as Visiting Professor, and McGill (~1987) as Birks Chair in Comparative Religion.

Asanga Tilakaratne works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served at the University of Kelaniya as Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy, and held posts as Department Head (attested 1993) and Professor (attested 2006) at the PGIPBS.
Asatoshi Kamiya, a scholar in Buddhist studies, earned an M.A. from Komazawa University. He held a post as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School (attested 1978).
Asef Bayat studied at the University of Kent (~1980–1984). He held posts at Leiden University (2000–2010) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2010).
Asen Balikci studied at Columbia University (~1957–1962). He held a post at Université de Montréal (~1969–1994).

Ashby Butnor works in philosophy and japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of Hawaii under Vrinda Dalmiya (-2009) and served as Visiting Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver (attested 2011).

Ashok Aklujkar works in indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as a professor at the University of British Columbia from ~1969 to ~1995.
Ashok Kumar Malhotra works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the East-West Center and founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.
Ashok Vajpeyi studied at St. Stephen's College, Delhi, where he completed an MA (~1961–1963). He is associated with indology and other fields.

Asim Kumar Chatterjee works in history, archaeology, and indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Calcutta (~1962–1967) under D. Mukherjee. He was a Senior Research Fellow there (attested 1970) and lecturer in English at Jangipur College.

Indologist and linguist Asko Parpola studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held posts at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1968), Academy of Finland (1982, 1989–1990), and University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

Asutosh Mookerjee worked in history, archaeology, and indology. He studied at South Suburban School, Presidency University, and University of Calcutta. He held a post at Calcutta High Court (1904) and served at the University of Calcutta (1906–1914; President 1921–1923).
Atsuhiko Yoshida works in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Seikei University and the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957), and held a post at Seikei University (~1978–2002).
Atsushi Ibuki works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1978–1988) and held a post as professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Atsushi Kanazawa works in indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1981). He was a lecturer at Meteorological College (~1983–1990) and held posts, including assistant professor, at Komazawa University (~1993–2004).
